reason: The cited evidence does not directly address atomic mobility, local compositional fluctuations, or premelting in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles. E1–E3 discuss bulk alloy solidification and phase separation, E4 describes kinetic limitations during synthesis of different HEA nanoparticles, E5 discusses laser heating of noble metal nanoparticles, and E6 shows homogeneous element distribution in CrMnFeCoNi nanoparticles, which contradicts the premise of local compositional fluctuations. None of the cited passages support the specific mechanistic claims about premelting behavior.
premises: Intrinsic lattice disorder in HEA nanoparticles limits atomic mobility during heating
Limited atomic mobility produces local compositional fluctuations
Local compositional fluctuations create regions with lower bonding strength
Lower-bonding-strength regions initiate local melting before the whole particle melts
This leads to a broader melting transition than in single-component nanoparticles
